dedupe_keys.name: sinalize forced outages maintenance registry and climate exposure of power transformers in brazil s national grid

description: SINALIZE is a data set for failure prediction and predictive maintenance of power transformers in Brazil's National Interconnected System (SIN), operated by the National Electric System Operator (ONS). The current version was published on Zenodo in September 2026 by Rodrigo Guimarães and covers January 2020 to July 2026. It holds 18,431 forced outage records with start and end times, duration, outage type and cause classification; 14,676 maintenance outage records; a registry of 1,698 transformers with commissioning date, substation arrangement, voltages, operating and owning agents and equipment type; and daily climate series from the NASA POWER service (temperature, precipitation, wind speed and gust, humidity and dew point) for the grid cells covering the equipment. Equipment, agents and locations are pseudonymised, with a data dictionary. Coverage is Brazil's interconnected grid. Files are CSV (semicolon separated, no header) and a Markdown dictionary, downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: coordinates are removed, so exposure is only available through anonymised climate cells, and this version drops the load series of the previous one. Simulation uses are weather-related transformer failure modelling, outage rate estimation and asset management studies. Related records: data-brazil-open-energy gives other open data on Brazil's power system.
